assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal benefit; the physiological discovery of a gut hormone with insulinotropic, satiety and gastric effects translated into one of the most consequential drug classes in decades.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and actions, GLP-2), Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible trio; Habener and others, and industry contributors such as Knudsen, are not available or are less academic, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is established by large independent trials and wide use; the basic science is decades old, so recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over who first identified the active GLP-1 peptide and its therapeutic potential
Whether industry scientists such as Knudsen should displace an academic laureate
Long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being characterized

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has reshaped circuit analysis across systems, including motor circuits; the originality of microbial opsins as genetically encoded actuators and the breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), the neuronal demonstration (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier concepts (Miesenboeck) are intertwined; six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so any trio omits deserving contributors. Deisseroth for the broad tool development, with Nagel and Hegemann for the molecular discovery, is a defensible but imperfect configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently validated for over fifteen years; clinical translation is early, but the experimental impact is mature.
uncertainties: Unavoidable exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck
Whether the prize should recognize the tool or the channelrhodopsin discovery
Human therapeutic application is still limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality in cancer immunotherapy with several approved products.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulation), Sadelain (CAR design and costimulation, preclinical proof) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early CAR trials) cover the main lines; Eshhar and others sit outside the credited list, and credit among these three is reasonably clear.
assessment.maturity: Clinical benefit is confirmed in multiple independent trials and approvals; toxicity and limited efficacy in solid tumors are ongoing issues but do not undermine the core achievement.
uncertainties: Priority relative to Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work, not in the credited names
Rosenberg versus alternative third laureates
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer and cancer, with population-level evidence of near-elimination of disease in vaccinated cohorts; a clear, original and lasting preventive-medicine breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer contributed to the Queensland VLP technology and early translation. Other groups (Zhou, Kirnbauer, Rose) also contributed to VLP formation, so the configuration is not free of dispute, but these three are well supported by the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Registry and effectiveness data from many countries show strong, independent confirmation; recognition after zur Hausen's 2008 prize on HPV and cervical cancer is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over VLP self-assembly among several groups
Zhou's contribution, deceased and not in the credited list
Relationship to the earlier HPV-cancer prize may be seen as incremental

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition turned CML from a fatal leukemia into a chronic manageable disease and validated targeted, mechanism-based cancer therapy; the principle was foundational for kinase-inhibitor oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis), Druker (preclinical and clinical demonstration of selectivity and efficacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) is a coherent trio. Rowley and others laid the BCR-ABL groundwork but are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of follow-up confirm durable survival; the discovery has been strongly validated, with Lasker recognition already given.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is regarded as translational drug development more than discovery
Sawyers versus other contributors such as Buchdunger or Zimmermann (not credited)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infantile disease; it is a mechanism-driven RNA therapeutic of high originality and clinical clarity.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory mechanism and the ISS-N1 target strategy, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development with Ionis; Singh and others made intermediate contributions. A two-person prize is cleanly supported by the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is shown by randomized trials and real-world data; the modality is relatively recent, but impact on neurology and RNA therapeutics is already substantial.
uncertainties: Credit shared with the Singh, Hua and Biogen team outside the credited list
Industry-led development may weigh against it for some members
Long-term durability and treatment of older patients is still being studied

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Anti-TNF therapy demonstrated that targeting a single cytokine can treat rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory diseases, establishing the biologics era in immunology with massive global benefit.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini together identified TNF as a driver in RA synovium and conducted the first clinical trials of blockade; the pair is a natural and well-documented configuration, though Vilcek, Cerami and Beutler did earlier TNF biology.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is confirmed by decades of independent trials and use; Lasker 2003 recognition indicates mature community acceptance.
uncertainties: Relative role of TNF discoverers outside the credited names
Possible perception that the contribution is therapeutic application of earlier cytokine biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation provided the leading cellular model of synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory; the discovery is original, foundational and has shaped decades of neurobiology, though the link from LTP to memory in vivo remains partly inferential.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo reported LTP in the hippocampus in 1973; Collingridge established NMDA receptor dependence, while Morris linked NMDA-dependent plasticity to spatial learning. Four credited names exceed three, so one important contributor is left out.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across laboratories and preparations over fifty years; recognition is long overdue rather than premature, but the causal relation to memory is still debated.
uncertainties: Choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third place
Evidence connecting LTP to memory storage remains partly correlative
Heterogeneity of LTP mechanisms across synapses
